items.title: Make the loading state show unmistakable progress
items.what: On the ShoeMoney pre-boot screen, the long bar beneath “Downloading the game” appears as a nearly empty dark brown hairline, with no clearly visible filled portion or percentage. The player can read that the game is downloading but cannot tell whether it is advancing or stalled.
items.why: This is the first screen a player sees, and an ambiguous loader makes a browser game feel frozen or unreliable before they have played.
items.how: Render a high-contrast gold fill inside the existing track from 0–100%, animate it only from real asset progress, and add a compact numeric state such as “Downloading 62%” or “Preparing dojo…” above the bar. Keep the warm palette, but ensure the fill differs clearly from the unfilled track at phone brightness.

items.title: Fix the landscape layout’s enormous unused control area
items.what: In the 1280×800 landscape gameplay screenshot, the dojo ends around y=570, leaving a large nearly black lower band. The stance and technique controls sit as small circles in the extreme lower corners, separated by roughly a thousand pixels of empty space.
items.why: A player who rotates their phone gets tiny, edge-hugging touch targets and loses a large amount of usable screen area. It looks like the game failed to reflow rather than intentionally adapting to landscape.
items.how: Add a dedicated landscape layout: extend the arena farther down, scale each stick to at least the current portrait touch diameter, and anchor the sticks inset from the lower-left and lower-right safe areas. Use the freed center-bottom space for the control legend or contextual move feedback rather than an empty black field.

items.title: Stop the persistent control legend from covering the fight space
items.what: During portrait gameplay, the wide “STANCE / TECHNIQUE” instruction card occupies the band immediately above both sticks, from roughly y=866 to y=953. It overlays the tatami directly below the fighters and remains present in multiple active-fight screenshots.
items.why: The card competes with the fighters and move-result feedback for the player’s lower-screen attention, while repeating information already expressed by the directional arrows on the two controls. In a fast touch game, that is visual obstruction where a player is looking for spacing and foot position.
items.how: Show this card only for the first few seconds of the first bout, then collapse it into a small tappable “?” beside MOVES. On later bouts, reveal a single short contextual hint only after an unused input or pause, and let the arena run cleanly from the fighters down to the controls.

items.title: Make the move-list input recipes readable at phone size
items.what: On the TECHNIQUES screen, every move recipe is represented by two small outlined circular direction icons, a tiny plus sign, then the move name. The controls are packed tightly into rows, while the pale-blue directional glyphs and gray “mid · Half point” metadata are comparatively low-contrast against the brown panel.
items.why: The move list is where a new player learns the central combat system. If they cannot quickly decode which stick directions to combine, they will return to play without understanding how to intentionally perform techniques.
items.how: Enlarge the input diagrams and color-code the first input as stance blue and the second as technique gold, matching the live controls. Increase the metadata contrast, add a one-line header such as “Hold stance direction + flick technique direction,” and make each row tappable to play a short silent in-panel input animation rather than relying solely on static icons.

items.title: Remove the orphaned record message from Settings
items.what: The SETTINGS screen has six options in the upper third, then almost the entire lower screen is empty. At the very bottom, below a divider, it says “No bouts yet — your record starts with your first fight.” This reads as an unrelated record panel stranded inside Settings.
items.why: The empty space and unrelated footer make the settings screen feel unfinished, and the player has no clear destination for viewing their actual match record once bouts exist.
items.how: Move the record status to a dedicated Profile/Record entry reachable from the main fight flow, or replace the footer with settings-specific content such as version/build and reset controls. If no additional settings are planned, shorten the panel to its content height so the close action and options form a deliberate, complete sheet.
